Ukraine says drones hit Russia’s gas heartland over 3,000 km from its border—a wartime record
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:39:56 UTC
01:39:56 KST

Ukraine's Special Operations Forces (SSO) said the 9 September operation struck the Purovsky and Novy Urengoy gas processing plants in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug.
Kyiv's earlier energy campaign concentrated on oil refineries and export hubs in western Russia. The new operation shifts the target set toward Siberian gas processing and challenges the protection once provided by distance, although its effect on production remains unknown. The SSO said drones operated by its Deep Strike units traveled more than 3,000 kilometers, making the operation Ukraine's deepest strike of the war.
Both the Purovsky and Novy Urengoy plants feed Russia's fuel and petrochemical industries. Ukraine's broader deep-strike campaign aims to cut the revenue and supplies sustaining Moscow's war.
Fire Point, the Ukrainian manufacturer of the FP-1, identified the drones as FP-1s and put the distance to the Novy Urengoy plant at more than 3,200 kilometers. The company reported a hit on the plant grounds but did not describe the damage.
Russian authorities have not confirmed the full Ukrainian account. Yamalo-Nenets Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said Russian forces had repelled the attack, according to The Times. Falling drone debris nevertheless caused a fire at an industrial facility in Novy Urengoy, he said.
Artyukhov reported no injuries but did not identify the facility. Russian officials have not acknowledged any strike on Purovsky.
Fire Point put the Novy Urengoy plant's annual design capacity at up to 19.5 million metric tons of raw material.
CyberBoroshno, a Ukrainian group that analyzes public imagery and data, said the strike hit a gas-processing unit at Gazprom Processing's Urengoy plant. Dnipro OSINT shared the analysis.
Gas condensate is a liquid produced alongside natural gas. The reported target separates ethane-rich gases from it. Those gases can be used to make polyethylene, a common plastic. CyberBoroshno said damage to the unit could disrupt supplies to a nearby chemical plant. Neither its identification of the unit nor the extent of the damage has been independently verified.
At Purovsky, the SSO reported damage but did not identify the equipment hit. Owned by Russian gas producer Novatek, the plant processes condensate into fuels and raw materials for the petrochemical industry. It processed 13.4 million metric tons in 2025, according to the SSO.
The effect on production at either plant remains unknown, as does whether any damage will be lasting.
The wider campaign
Ukraine's deep-strike units repeatedly struck Novatek's Ust-Luga gas-condensate complex on the Baltic Sea. Ukraine says drones hit two Siberian gas plants over 3,000 km from its border earlier in 2026. The facility processes stabilized gas condensate and has a design capacity of over 6 million metric tons a year, according to the General Staff.
A 31 March attack briefly halted port operations, while the 14 August strike was the sixth attack on the port that year. Ukraine has not disclosed how much production those attacks disrupted.

'Illegal, provocative': Arab countries condemn Netanyahu's incursion into Syria's Mount Hermon
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:39:25 UTC
01:39:25 KST

Several Arab countries have condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s illegal entry into Syria’s Mount Hermon and urged the UN Security Council to take action to halt attacks on the sovereignty of the Arab country.
Netanyahu entered the occupied Syrian area of Mount Hermon on Wednesday accompanied by Defence Minister Israel Katz, in a move that observers viewed as part of his campaign ahead of Knesset elections scheduled for October 27.
In a statement on Thursday, the Kuwaiti Foreign Ministry strongly condemned Netanyahu’s “illegal entry” into Syrian territory, describing it as a “flagrant violation” of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a “blatant breach” of international law.
It said continued Israeli incursions and attacks inside Syrian territory represented an “escalation that undermined security and stability in the region.”
It also demanded that the UN Security Council fulfil its responsibilities by stopping the attacks and ensuring Israel’s compliance with relevant international resolutions, stressing the need to respect the 1974 Agreement on Disengagement of Forces between Syria and Israel.
Similarly, Qatar strongly condemned Netanyahu’s “illegal entry” into Syrian territory and crossing of international borders.
The foreign ministry said it constituted a “blatant violation” of the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and a “flagrant breach” of international law.
The ministry urged the international community to take urgent action to compel Israel to comply with international resolutions, particularly the 1974 Agreement on Disengagement of Forces, and to halt its repeated attacks on Syrian territory.
Saudi Arabia also condemned in the strongest terms the “illegal entry” as a “flagrant violation” of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and a blatant breach of international law.
In a statement, the Saudi foreign ministry stressed the need for Israel to “halt its violations and actions against Syrian territory and to comply with the 1974 Agreement on Disengagement of Forces to preserve regional security and stability.”
‘Provocative’
Separately, Egypt condemned the “repeated Israeli incursions” into Syrian territory.
In a statement, the foreign ministry rejected all Israeli violations and incursions, warning that “continued escalation could fuel tensions and undermine regional security and stability.”
It reaffirmed Egypt’s full solidarity with Syria and support for its sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity.
The Syrian foreign ministry on Wednesday also condemned Netanyahu’s “illegal entry” as a “provocative” move and a violation of its sovereignty, territorial integrity and international law.
Jordan’s foreign ministry called the “flagrant violation” of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity a “blatant breach” of international law.
In a video filmed during his visit, Netanyahu, wearing a bulletproof vest, said he was standing at the summit of Mount Hermon on the eve of the Jewish New Year, pointing to Damascus, Lebanon and the Syrian Golan Heights.
Netanyahu claimed Israel had established unprecedented “absolute control” over the area stretching from Mount Hermon towards the Yarmouk River.
He said Israel would not allow “terrorist forces” to establish a presence near its borders.
Katz, meanwhile, signaled that Israel intended to maintain its occupation of the area. “We are here on Mount Hermon, and we will not move from here,” he said in a separate video.
Israel has occupied Syria’s Golan Heights since 1967 and unilaterally annexed the territory in 1981, a move not recognized by the international community.

Don’t strawman the argument
While I appreciate that Gerhard Erasmus, an expert in Taiwan’s educational field, took the time to respond to my letter, I would like to clarify what I said.
The phrase “children are like sponges” was meant to highlight something specific: Someone exposed to a language continuously from a young age would generally have a much stronger grasp of it by adulthood than someone with little or no exposure who has to begin learning it at an older age.
Research on additional-language acquisition has consistently shown the importance of sustained exposure to a second or additional language. That does not mean there are not challenges that also need to be recognized and addressed.
If Taiwan develops a genuine bilingual education system from a young age, students would enter university with a stronger foundation in Mandarin and English. They could continue their education in Taiwan, primarily in a Mandarin environment, while developing the ability to understand and use increasingly complex academic concepts in both languages.
That is very different from expecting university professors to bring students up to a required level of English before they can teach their subject using complex English.
I did not state that Taiwan should simply copy Ontario’s French-immersion system. I used it as an example of how students can receive substantial education in a second language while continuing to learn and function in their primary language. Ontario demonstrated that students can continue into fully French-language universities and programs. Experts, such as Erasmus, could take what they learned from Canada and other countries and develop a uniquely Taiwanese public bilingual education framework.
I also did not state that someone with a Bachelor of Arts degree and a Teaching English as a Foreign Language certificate is academically or professionally equivalent to a fully certified teacher, such as someone with a Bachelor of Education or a Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages qualification. My point was that Taiwan already has a pool of local and foreign English-language teachers with degrees, English proficiency and classroom experience. Some might have exceptional teaching ability. Rather than dismissing teachers because they do not yet possess every qualification required by the Ministry of Education, Taiwan could invest in those who demonstrate the ability and willingness to become more qualified teachers.
Bilingual 2030 needs a proper structure from primary education through secondary and higher education to become a reality, and I see professionals such as Erasmus and from other disciplines making this a reality.
Paul Garrelfs
Toronto

Beijing is losing its diplomatic composure
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:11 UTC
01:38:11 KST

While discussing the South China Sea and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) at the Seoul Defense Dialogue on Tuesday, Philippine Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr received a memo from a military attache at the Chinese embassy in Seoul.
The note reiterated China’s position on the 2016 arbitration ruling — an international legal decision that said China’s “nine-dash line” claim had no legal basis under UNCLOS — that it is “illegal,” “invalid” and nonbinding.
Rather than pocketing the memo, an exasperated-looking Teodoro read it aloud line-by-line to the audience and rebutted each point.
China perhaps hoped to use the memo to force its position into an international forum. Instead, Teodoro put it on display and criticized the move as indecent.
“This is not gray zone anymore,” but rather “coercion, bullying and aggression,” he said.
If a country that calls itself a “great power” truly had sufficient confidence and international influence, why would it feel the need to interrupt someone’s remarks with a memo at a multilateral security forum held in another country? A truly great power relies on institutions, arguments and the power of persuasion; a nation with true substance has no need for petty tactics to prove its strength.
Viewed from this perspective, what that memo revealed to the world was not China’s power, but its deep concern and anxiety over others discussing the South China Sea.
Diplomacy has never been about deriving power from the volume of your voice, nor does a more hardline stance necessarily earn greater respect. Particularly in multilateral settings, true strength often lies in exercising restraint. You may disagree with others, lodge stern protests or present legal arguments, but if you cannot even exercise basic judgement over what is appropriate in a given setting, what would ultimately suffer is your own image.
What is all the more intriguing is that Teodoro chose not to handle the matter privately. He instead made the memo public, turning what China had intended as a behind-the-scenes pressure tactic into a diplomatic lesson shone under the full glare of public scrutiny.
This might have well been the memo’s greatest backfire. If China truly wished to become a great power respected by others, it should understand that true greatness lies not in the number of warships a state possesses, the size of its economy or its ability to silence others — rather, it lies in whether, when confronted with dissenting views, it can maintain sufficient confidence and magnanimity.
Although a piece of paper might be small, it can reveal the scale of the diplomatic landscape. This time, China might have intended to put the Philippines in its place, but it instead put Teodoro in the international spotlight and allowed him to turn the memo into a “souvenir” of China’s diplomatic posture, for all to refer to.
By attempting to use a petty gesture to establish the dominance of a great power, China showed the world a level of immaturity and loss of composure that no “great power” should display.
Lin Cheng-wu is a junior-high school teacher.
Translated by Kyra Gustavsen

Health rewards program’s lessons
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:09 UTC
01:38:09 KST

The Ministry of Sports has launched its “sweat rewards” program, in which participants who meet any of the weekly requirements — exercising for at least 30 minutes in a single session, accumulating at least 8,000 steps a day, walking or running at least 5km in a single session or cycling at least 15km — could receive a NT$50 voucher each week. The program runs for 14 weeks.
I had assumed that few people would participate in the program. To my surprise, many of my colleagues began sharing information about it in our group chat. By Sunday last week, everyone had uploaded records showing that they had walked 8,000 steps during the first week.
Just days ago, I used my voucher at a convenience store and uploaded my exercise record for the second week. Over the next 12 weeks, my colleagues and I plan to continue encouraging each other to persevere, with the goal of developing regular exercise habits and maintaining our health.
I believe that the sports ministry’s exercise incentive program has been quite successful so far. After all, getting people to actually exercise and develop regular workout habits is by far more effective than simply repeating slogans or releasing promotional materials.
By comparison, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications’ new “zero traffic infringements” prize draw for motorcycle riders places greater emphasis on publicity, with evidently weaker substantive results. Under the transportation ministry’s lottery — launched in honor of Traffic Safety Month — those who own a motorcycle with a valid license plate are eligible to enter as long as they have no record of traffic law infringements or accidents while on the road.
Although there are 800 prizes, including a grand prize of a large heavy-duty motorcycle worth about NT$280,000, the odds of winning are low. That could discourage public participation, making the campaign a mere formality in which publicity outweighs any actual impact.
The transportation ministry should follow the sports ministry’s example: launch a program to encourage the public to obey traffic rules and keep it running for one to two years or even longer. Motorcycle riders could register once every quarter, with those who meet eligibility requirements receiving bonus vouchers. Alternatively, the transportation ministry could adopt a system similar to the invoice lottery, with a drawing every two months.
A campaign built around the principle that everyone who obeys traffic laws is a winner would give people a tangible incentive to participate and make the program more meaningful.
Chen Hung-hui is a military instructor and university life resources officer.
Translated by Kyra Gustavsen

====================================================================================================

The world that the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks did not make
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:09 UTC
01:38:09 KST

Today marks the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 (9/11), terrorist attacks on the US. For many Americans, 9/11 is a distant memory, or not a memory at all — approximately 40 percent of the US population was either born after the attacks or is too young to remember them.
On that day, 19 terrorists took control of four civilian aircraft, flew two into the towers of New York’s World Trade Center, struck the Pentagon with a third and crashed the fourth in a Pennsylvania field after passengers physically prevented the terrorists from reaching their target, often thought to be the White House or another government building in Washington.
All 19 hijackers were from the Middle East, 15 from Saudi Arabia. All were trained in Afghanistan and four at US flight schools as part of an operation planned, organized and carried out by al-Qaeda (“the base”), the terrorist group founded by Osama bin Laden.
By the day’s end, close to 3,000 men, women and children had been killed and more than 6,000 injured. Most were American, although citizens of more than 100 countries lost their lives as well.
To invoke former US president Franklin D. Roosevelt’s description of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, 9/11, too, was “a date which will live in infamy.”
However, with the fading of personal recollections, it seems right and necessary to ask the question: Did 9/11 mark a turning point? Or was it a day that, as tragic as it was, did not alter the course of history?
The truth is closer to the latter. Fortunately, 9/11 did not usher in an age defined by terrorism. A wave of attacks on a similar scale did not follow, in no small part because the US and other governments adopted measures that made it more difficult for would-be terrorists to emerge and succeed.
Another reason 9/11 did not alter history is that terrorists tend to be better at destroying than building, at killing rather than creating. As a result, they leave no lasting legacy.
By no means is this meant to imply that 9/11 did not matter. It led directly to military intervention in Afghanistan, where US-led forces, in coordination with Afghan tribesmen, ousted the ruling Taliban, which had provided sanctuary to bin Laden and the terrorists who carried out the attacks.
Call it what it was: regime change.
However, what followed, something that was closer to nation-building, provided an early lesson: Removing a regime from power is one thing, replacing it with a better system that endures and governs effectively is quite another — and far more difficult.
Twenty-five years later, after more than 800,000 US soldiers had been deployed, more than US$2 trillion spent and more than 2,400 Americans killed in combat (along with another 1,100 soldiers from NATO countries and others), Afghanistan is again ruled by the Taliban.
In March 2003, just a year and a half after 9/11, the US initiated a war of choice against Iraq. It is possible, but unlikely, that this war would have happened absent 9/11. In the wake of the attacks, then-US president George W. Bush and many of his closest advisers became determined to demonstrate that the US was much more than a victim. (I served in the Bush administration during this time, but opposed the war in Iraq and resigned soon after.)
Some in the Bush administration believed that Saddam Hussein, Iraq’s strongman leader, was developing or even possessed a nuclear weapon and feared that terrorists would get ahold of one. Others were taken with the idea of spreading democracy to Iraq and the region, an outcome that would have made the region less likely to produce terrorists and support terrorism. Almost all of this turned out to be wrong.
However, the costly war (more than 4,000 US soldiers lost their lives and trillions more dollars were spent) turned many Americans against overseas involvement and eventually positioned Iran, which had nothing to do with 9/11 even if it was a strategic beneficiary of the war, as a major power in the Middle East.
Iran played a larger role in terrorism in the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas on Israel, resulting in the deaths of more than 800 civilians, but again, as awful as that was, little of what has happened since, be it in Gaza, Lebanon or Iran, was preordained or can be attributed to terrorism. Rather, subsequent developments largely reflect policy decisions taken in the first instance by Israel and the US.
Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that 9/11 was not a transformative event. Far more important were China’s rise, Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, the COVID-19 pandemic, the collective failure to take meaningful action against climate change, the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and, perhaps more than anything else, the US’ rejection of the post-war order that it had a large hand in building.
These truths do not diminish the lesson that should be drawn. Although 9/11 did not usher in an age of terrorism, we are not safe from it. On the contrary, we have entered an era in which AI, along with accurate, inexpensive, and destructive drones and advances in bioengineering, have given terrorists more opportunity than ever to impose large-scale harm at minimal cost. The goal must be to ensure that they do not succeed and that terrorism remains at most a limited problem.
Richard Haass, president emeritus of the Council on Foreign Relations, is a senior counselor at Centerview Partners, distinguished university scholar at New York University, and the author of the weekly Substack newsletter Home & Away.

Brazil Supreme Court moves to end bitter judges’ feud
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:08 UTC
01:38:08 KST

The Brazilian Supreme Court president on Wednesday attempted to end a crisis in the court by suspending a series of conflicting rulings by rival judges that have dominated a bitter election campaign.
The court is reeling from a scandal involving the alleged links between leading Justice Alexandre de Moraes and a disgraced banker charged with massive fraud.
The case has descended into open warfare between Moraes, who famously led the coup investigation into former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, and fellow Justice Andre Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee.
Photo: EPA
On Tuesday, the country’s top policeman, Andrei Rodrigues, was swept up in the infighting, when he was suspended by Mendonca, who accused the police of spying on him.
A day later a third justice, Flavio Dino, a former minister under Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, reinstated the head of the federal police.
Brazilian Supreme Court President Edson Fachin promptly waded into the dispute and suspended both rulings, according to a ruling seen by Agence France-Presse.
Fachin gave Rodrigues 48 hours to provide information before deciding his fate.
The eruption in the court has overshadowed the run-up to next month’s presidential election, in which Bolsonaro’s senator son, Flavio Bolsonaro, is trying to unseat Lula.
Mendonca fired the opening salvo in the row by ordering the publication last week of text messages from banker Daniel Vorcaro to Moraes, asking for information about the case against him.
Moraes hit back, accusing Mendonca of abuse of power on the basis of confidential police intelligence reports, whereupon Mendonca suspended Rodrigues.
The texts from Vorcaro, whose private bank Banco Master collapsed last year in a multibillion-dollar pool of debt, have become fodder in the presidential race.
Lula on Wednesday said “greater transparency” was needed in the case, as well as an end to “selective leaks that impact the electoral race.”
“It is urgent to fully lift the secrecy of the investigations into all those involved in the Master case, whoever they may be, no matter who it hurts. Brazil needs to know the truth,” he wrote on X.
Vorcaro had boasted of having “friends in all branches of government” before becoming embroiled in one of Brazil’s biggest-ever financial scandals.
The Master case is a “toxic” affair, a Supreme Court source said, adding that police suspect the banker “put money into various places in order to later collect favors.”
In the days leading up to his arrest in November, Vorcaro sent about 30 text messages to a phone number police say belonged to Moraes.
“Do you think I need to be out of the country as early as Monday?” he asked in one message, just before his arrest while boarding a private jet.
Flavio Bolsonaro has pounced on the texts to bash Moraes, a hate figure for the Brazilian and US right for having spearheaded the coup trial of his father.
Jair Bolsonaro, an ally of US President Donald Trump, is serving a 27-year jail sentence after he was convicted of trying to cling to power after losing the 2022 election to Lula.
However, Flavio Bolsonaro’s own links to Vorcaro have been questioned after it emerged that the banker transferred millions of dollars to an intermediary at the senator’s request.
The younger Bolsonaro said the money was intended for use toward a film about his father.
The scandal engulfing the Supreme Court has sown alarm in the Brazilian business community.
About 3,000 business organizations released a manifesto on Wednesday, warning of an “extremely serious institutional crisis.”
“If the legitimacy [of the judges] is questioned, everything else becomes uncertain: legal certainty, trust in institutions, and even social peace,” they said.

Environmentalists blast officials over port project
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:08 UTC
01:38:08 KST

Environmental advocates in Taichung yesterday filed a criminal report accusing 17 current and former officials of forgery to shield a Port of Taichung land reclamation project from environmental and ecological assessments.
The advocates filed the report at the Taichung District Prosecutors’ Office and urged the Executive Yuan to halt the project in line with a 34,000-signature petition to protect the habitat of critically endangered Taiwanese humpback dolphins.
Former and current officials of Taiwan International Ports Corp and its Taichung branch, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, the Ocean Affairs Council and its Ocean Conservation Administration, and the Ministry of Environment are named in the complaint, Government Watch Alliance executive director Hsu Hsin-hsin (許心欣) said.
Photo courtesy of the Ocean Conservation Administration
The groups involved, including the Taichung branch of the ports company and the transportation ministry, claimed that the project was part of the 2017-2021 Future Development and Construction Plan for International Commercial Ports, which was approved before waters in the region on Aug. 31, 2020, were listed as a “major wildlife habitat” of the dolphins, Hsu said.
The listing took effect the day after on Sept. 1, 2020.
That is why the council determined that the project was not subject to a critical habitat assessment review, she said.
However, the revision of the project was approved on Sept. 21, 2020, after the critical habitat listing, she said.
The groups claimed that the fill and seawall project was part of the Taichung Port Offshore Wind Power Industry Zone — involving wharf work to serve the offshore-wind industry — making it an “existing development,” which is clearly impossible given that the fill project has a NT$10.4 billion (US$329.66 million) budget, but the wharf project’s was NT$2.8 billion, Hsu said.
The groups seem to have used incorrect information to deceive the council, which might have caused a public official to make a false entry, Hsu said.
The council might be guilty of malfeasance if it knew that the habitat listing was issued before the third revision of the land reclamation project, but did not order an ecological assessment, she said, adding the transportation ministry seems to have falsely endorsed the land reclamation project.
The materials approved to reclaim land were changed to construction surplus soil and rock, despite the risk of heavy metal pollution, she said.
However, the environmental ministry, and the council and Ocean Conservation Administration failed to order the land reclamation project to undergo additional environmental assessments, she said.
The unusually low fee of NT$450 per cubic meter for material to use in the reclamation project indicates that the three central governmental agencies might have facilitated profiteering, Hsu added.

Unknown

2026-09-10
16:38:07 UTC
01:38:07 KST

The Philippines yesterday deployed coast guard, military and civilian vessels in a race to find survivors on a smoldering passenger-and-cargo ferry off the western island of Palawan, after a fire on board killed at least five people and left 86 missing.
Drone footage released by the Philippine Coast Guard showed the blackened MV June Aster surrounded by clear blue-green waters, with the vessel still generating smoke hours after the fire broke out on Wednesday night.
Philippine Coast Guard spokeswoman Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said thick smoke continued to billow from the vessel, while extreme heat and the risk of explosions prevented rescuers from boarding.
Photo: Philippine Coast Guard via EPA
So far 43 people, including two Chilean nationals, have been rescued from the ferry, which was on a voyage from Baseco in Manila to Coron, a popular tourist destination in Palawan known for its diving sites and island-hopping attractions.
The coast guard had deployed two 44m vessels and three smaller craft, while army rescue boats, local fishers and private resort owners had joined the search since Wednesday night, Cayabyab said.
One military aircraft was also on standby, she said.
Photo: Philippine Coast Guard via AP
At least one survivor reported hearing a loud explosion from the cargo hold before the blaze, Cayabyab told a news conference.
“After that there was smoke and fire. As per the testimony of the survivor, it escalated quickly. After seconds, the fire started spreading,” she said.
The survivor described it as a powerful blast, but authorities have yet to determine what caused it, she said.
Cayabyab said some survivors pulled from the sea were not wearing life jackets, suggesting passengers might have jumped overboard as the fire spread.
According to the vessel’s manifest, the ferry was carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members and had a maximum capacity of 330 people.
The vessel had passed safety inspections, Cayabyab said.
It was also carrying five motorcycles, an electric vehicle, a forklift, a pickup truck and mostly cargo goods, she said.
Of the 43 rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, she said.
The identity of another survivor was not immediately clear.
“Most of the people we rescued were those who had been swimming away from the vessel,” Cayabyab said.
Many were in a state of shock, and comprehensive interviews that could shed light on the incident would only take place later, she said.
Asked whether authorities were looking at possible sabotage or a terrorist attack, she said it was too early to draw conclusions and that the investigation was ongoing.
The vessel’s owner, Atienza Inter-Island Ferries, said it was fully cooperating with government authorities investigating the incident.
“We are working around the clock and have mobilized all available resources to manage this crisis,” the company said in a statement, adding that it was committed to transparency as the investigation progressed.

Livestock institute touts egg white processing method
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:05 UTC
01:38:05 KST

The Taiwan Livestock Research Institute has developed a technique to repurpose salted egg white as food ingredients, with projections showing it could add more than NT$10 million (US$316,977) to the annual output of the domestic salted egg yolk processing industry.
The industry produces more than 4,300 tonnes of salted egg white each year as a by-product. While salted egg yolk is commonly used in pastries, including mooncakes, most salted egg whites are discarded due to their high salt content of up to 9 percent, institute director-general Huang Jeng-fang (黃振芳) said.
The new technique helped lower the salinity to 1.5 percent or less, with dietary fiber added to boost the processed nutritional value of egg whites, Huang said.
Photo: Yang Yuan-ting, Taipei Times
Wu Ling-tsai (吳鈴彩), an assistant researcher at the institute who led technical development of the project, said konjac powder was integrated into the egg white to increase the fiber content.
It took the research team five years to develop the technique, which brought down the sodium content to 453mg per 100g, about the same as a tea egg, Wu said.
Processed salted egg whites have higher nutritional value than the unprocessed by-product, with 9.9g of protein, 4.7g of dietary fiber, 0.3g of fat and nearly no sugar per 100g, she said.
More than 100 boxes of duck eggs were used during the technical development process, with each egg weighing about 18kg, she said.
The salted egg whites were used in large quantities to overcome konjac powder’s characteristic of being highly incompatible with proteins, Wu said.
Operational details of the technique can be adjusted to create different shapes and mouth sensations for different food products tailored to food processors’ needs, she said.
The ratio of salted egg white by-products and their processed egg white output is about one to one, she said.
With about 3 tonnes of salted egg white disposed of per month and processed protein products costing about NT$300 per kilogram, the processing technique is projected to add NT$10.8 million or more to the industry’s annual output, Wu said.
Duck Farmer Association vice president Ou Ling-ho (歐陵合) thanked the institute for helping “turn the hot potato into gold.”
Salted egg white by-products were used for pig feed, but the government banned feeding pigs with kitchen waste, Ou said.
The institute’s technique benefits food processing operators and has the potential to advance high-protein fitness foods for gym-goers, he said.
The technique was patented last year and won a silver prize at the second Taiwan Agricultural Sustainability Awards in Taipei on Wednesday.

Photo: CNA

Several European cities are replacing traditional white streetlights with red lighting to reduce light pollution and protect wildlife. In Copenhagen’s suburb of Gladsaxe, red LED lights have been installed along roads and cycle paths near bat habitats. The lights are placed at intervals that create darker gaps, allowing light-sensitive animals to cross safely without being exposed to predators and still providing enough visibility for people. Studies have shown that white and green light can reduce bat activity, whereas red light has little to no effect. Studies conducted in the Netherlands found that light-sensitive bats remain active under red lighting.

A UK clinical trial known as “Sentinel” is testing whether a small patch of skin from an organ donor can help detect lung transplant rejection at an earlier stage. The patch is grafted onto the patient’s forearm, making it possible to monitor visible changes such as rashes that may signal rejection before standard tests do. Scientists believe the skin may show signs of rejection earlier than other organs and is easier to observe directly. In one case, a patient who received a lung transplant in 2024 noticed a purple rash on the patch, which led doctors to detect mild rejection early

Syphilis cases rise 3% through August
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:38:00 UTC
01:38:00 KST

Syphilis cases in Taiwan rose by 3 percent year-on-year in the first eight months of this year, driven by a 4 percent increase among women and young adults, the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) said in a statement yesterday.
The CDC said that 78 percent of cases in the period were male, while 70 percent were aged 15 to 44.
Reported cases among women and people aged 15 to 24 were 1,538 and 1,340 respectively, both up 4 percent from the same period last year, it said.
Photo: Chen Chien-chih, Taipei Times
CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Min-cheng (林明誠) said there were 68 reported cases of congenital syphilis during the period, highlighting the need for measures to control the disease.
Infants can contract congenital syphilis if their mother was diagnosed with the disease while pregnant, but they must be monitored for up to 15 months before a definitive diagnosis can be made, Lin said.
The number of reported cases does not necessarily correspond to the number of diagnoses, she said, adding that some cases might be attributed to false-positive test results of mothers, with subsequent testing confirming that they did not have the disease.
If pregnant women diagnosed with syphilis do not seek timely treatment, it could lead to stillbirth, miscarriage or premature birth, she said.
Benzathine penicillin G is the only effective treatment for preventing mother-to-child transmission, she added.
Syphilis can be difficult to diagnose definitively, as it can be asymptomatic and can cause a variety of symptoms that might easily be mistaken for a common cold or other skin conditions, Lin said.
Symptoms can also temporarily subside without treatment, leading people to delay seeking medical care and assume that the infection has gone away, she said.
However, Treponema pallidum — the bacteria that causes the disease — can spread and remain transmissible in the body, potentially progressing to severe tertiary syphilis and allowing an unseen chain of transmission to persist, Lin said.
Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment are vital to stopping the spread, she said.
If pregnant women test positive in an initial rapid plasma reagin or venereal disease screening during prenatal care, the same blood sample can be used for a T pallidum particle agglutination or T Pallidum hemagglutination assay confirmatory test, eliminating the need for a return visit and helping speed diagnosis, reporting and treatment, the CDC said.
Pregnant women with positive initial screening results should undergo confirmatory testing as soon as possible and, if diagnosed with syphilis, undergo appropriate treatment promptly, it said.
When reporting cases involving pregnant women, medical professionals should also record the pregnancy and gestational age to facilitate follow-up by public health authorities, it added.

Europe’s center fears nationalist wave after AfD victory, but only has itself to blame
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:54 UTC
01:37:54 KST

The numbers speak for themselves: Alternative for Germany (AfD), a party that dabbles in Nazi imagery, distinguishes between “biological” and “passport” Germans, and is too extreme even for Marine le Pen, leader of the National Rally in France, nearly doubled its score in Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt to 43.8 percent of the vote.
Meanwhile, the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz collapsed to 17.2 percent, less than half its total in the same race five years ago and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) — Germany’s other main party of government for the past 60-odd years — scraped 9.3 percent.
The least that can be said is that the center did not hold.
Illustration: Mountain People
It is not yet clear whether the AfD, whose local branch in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt is officially classified by the country’s domestic intelligence service as “confirmed right-wing extremist,” will be able to form a government. It has 39 lawmakers in the 83-member parliament, just short of an outright majority.
However, the score is the party’s strongest-ever state result and puts it closer to governing a German state than any far-right party since World War II. It has sent shock waves around Europe, with nationalists cheering a “historic win” that is “just the beginning” and mainstream leaders warning of a “grave moment” for Europe.
Sweden holds legislative elections next weekend. France faces a crunch presidential ballot next spring. Key parliamentary races will follow there, as well as in Italy, Spain and Poland later in the year. Far-right parties are polling strongly in all of them and Europe’s center fears a continent-wide nationalist wave.
It would be wise not to read too much into one election result in one quite particular German state. Saxony-Anhalt, analysts say, is home to barely 1.8 million voters and has long been a far-right stronghold. In federal and state elections over the past decade, support for the AfD there has consistently been double the national average.
“A far-right party winning a regional election in Germany is not more scary than a far-right party winning a regional election in France, the UK or the Netherlands,” said Tarik Abou-Chadi, a professor of European politics at Oxford University. “Saxony-Anhalt should not be the basis for sweeping conclusions about the electoral sociology of the AfD.”
Nonetheless, the AfD leads in national polls. It is also ahead — although in a far tighter race, with the SPD — in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where state elections are due later this month, and it is lying second even in liberal Berlin. Its rise is part of a decade-long march by far-right parties across Europe.
Almost one in four voters in Europe now cast their ballot for far-right parties, according to research led by Matthijs Rooduijn, a political scientist at the University of Amsterdam, a proportion that has grown nearly fivefold since the mid-1990s and climbed particularly steeply over the past three years.
This analysis, by more than 150 political scientists in 31 countries, found that the proportion of Europeans voting for a far-right party in their country’s most recent national elections had risen this year to more than 23 percent, from about 10 percent a decade ago and roughly 5 percent in 1995.
Far-right populist parties are now in government as part of ruling coalitions in Croatia, the Czech Republic, Italy and Finland, propping up a right-wing minority government in Sweden, and leading in the polls in Austria, Belgium, France and Germany (and, until very recently, the UK).
They have also suffered recent defeats, including in the Netherlands, where Geert Wilders’ Freedom party (PVV) lost nearly one-third of its seats to finish second last year, and Hungary, where former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orban’s Fidesz was comprehensively beaten by his center-right rival in April.
However, the trend seems clear.
As Cas Mudde of the University of Georgia, a leading expert on Europe’s far right, put it after Orban’s defeat: “The far right is here to stay and many of its parties are as established as the [former] ‘mainstream’ parties. Like other parties, their electoral support fluctuates.”
That steady electoral advance has been achieved, despite a refusal by mainstream parties in countries such as France and Germany to collaborate with far-right parties, prompting some commentators to argue that the “cordon sanitaire” or “firewall” has now failed, or even been counterproductive.
By keeping the AfD out, they argue, Germany’s mainstream parties have actually boosted it. The party has been protected from the compromises and failures inherent in government. At the same time, the center has been “hollowed-out” — forced into uncomfortable, unstable alliances that agree on and, vitally, accomplish little, further frustrating voters and driving support for the extremes.
“There’s a self-reinforcing political dynamic that feeds the AfD’s rise,” said Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group risk consultancy. “The weaker the election results, the less common ground in the coalition, the fewer the policy results. The fewer results, the bigger the frustration in the electorate, the bigger the AfD’s share of the vote.”
However, many political scientists say that blaming the firewall is an excuse, and data suggest that far-right parties do not in any case get weaker when they are in government, but become stronger. One recent study of more than 1,300 different governments in 57 countries found far-right parties that entered government averaged a score 6 percentage points higher in the next election.
Besides the persistent inability of mainstream governments to deliver for disillusioned voters hit by a spiraling cost of living crisis, it is above all the gradual mainstreaming and normalization of the far right’s ideas that has driven — and continues to drive — its steady advance, political scientists argue.
Research suggests voter attitudes toward core far-right themes such as immigration have not changed significantly, but have become much more significant in their voting decisions: Normalization by the media and by mainstream parties that readily embrace far-right framing have legitimized far-right views.
“The entire debate about whether the cordon sanitaire is ‘successful’ or contributes to strengthening the far right completely misses the point,” said Gabriela Greilinger, an Austrian-Hungarian political scientist. “Far-right politics and policies already constantly take center stage, whether or not the far right is in power. There is no cordon around their ideas.”
Well, sort of. Tomorrow is the seventy-fifth anniversary of the San Francisco Peace Treaty, signed by forty-nine nations on September 8, 1951. The Republic of China wasn’t one of them. Article 2(b) of the Treaty reads: “Japan renounces all right, title and claim to Formosa and the Pescadores.” So, tomorrow would be the Diamond Jubilee of Formosa’s freedom from Japanese sovereignty. As my good friend and former Examination Yuan President Yao Chia-wen (姚嘉文) voiced in these pages last year (“San Francisco treaty should be taught: adviser”, Sept. 7, 2025), the Japan peace treaty should be taught in all Taiwan schools to

The Guatemalan Embassy celebrated the Central American country’s 205th independence day at a reception in Taipei on Thursday attended by Taiwanese officials and members of the diplomatic community.

Photo: CNA
He cited increases in Guatemalan exports to Taiwan, additional scholarships for Guatemalan students and efforts launched after President Bernardo Arevalo’s June 2025 visit, to help Guatemala play a role in the semiconductor supply chain.

Taiwan will encourage more companies to establish operations in Guatemala and use the country as a hub for expansion into the Americas, contributing to industrial development and job creation, Ger added.

City unveils GS safe pet product certification
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:53 UTC
01:37:53 KST

The New Taipei City Government on Tuesday unveiled a GS safety certificate system for pet products in collaboration with private enterprises in the industry.
Incidents involving animal harm by unsafe pet products prompted the city’s Animal Protection and Health Inspection Office to develop a safety labeling system based on policies that foreign countries successfully implemented, office Deputy Commissioner Liu Hsu-fen (劉淑芬) told a news conference.
Pet products using substandard materials or of poor construction pose a danger to pets, Liu said.
Photo courtesy of the New Taipei City Animal Protection and Health Inspection Office
A trolleys’ weight-bearing capacity, small components or sharp edges on toys and escape-proof fences are some of the design features that the GS standard evaluates before certifying a product, she said.
Establishing safety standards and inspection protocols helps manufacturers to design better products and identify potential flaws to prevent harm, said Huang Hsien-ping (黃獻平), chairman of the Taipei-based China Pet Products Development Association.
The GS standard obliges manufacturers to report unsafe products to the association for recall and comply with measures should a major safety incident occur, Huang said.
Office Director Yang Shu-fang (楊淑方) said pet owners should think carefully about their pet’s size, physical condition, age and habits before buying products.
Protecting the welfare of pets requires a regulatory system that provides comprehensive oversight from design to safety evaluation before products are released to the consumer market, an office spokesperson said.
New Taipei City Government officials and association representatives at the news conference demonstrated how to check the suitability of a product for pets.

Army to conduct another Tianma exercise
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:53 UTC
01:37:53 KST

The 6th Army Command is to conduct live-fire anti-armor drills in Hsinchu County from Wednesday to Friday next week for the second consecutive month of its “Tianma” (天馬) exercise as Taiwan’s anti-armor units step up training with newly fielded TOW 2B missiles.
Taiwan has received the full package it procured under its High-Performance Anti-Armor Missile Program, which includes 1,700 TOW 2B RF anti-armor missiles, 100 Improved Target Acquisition Systems and 100 M1167 High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicles, the Ministry of National Defense said.
The NT$11.815 billion (US$374.51 million) program, launched in 2018, aimed to bolster Taiwan’s asymmetric warfare capabilities.
Photo courtesy of the Military News Agency
The equipment has been distributed to military units, which have begun training and familiarizing themselves with the new systems, contributing to a higher tempo of live-fire exercises in recent months.
The Tianma exercise is the military’s major anti-armor live-fire exercise, and typically features TOW and Javelin missiles.
The exercises are usually conducted at coastal firing areas in Pingtung County, such as Fangshan (枋山), Jioupeng (九鵬) and Jialyutang (加祿堂), due to range and safety restrictions.
In line with the ministry’s push for combat-oriented training, the exercise this year was conducted at tactical positions within each combatant command’s area of responsibility, allowing troops to train in their designated operational areas and familiarize themselves with local terrain.
The command’s latest exercise is to be held at Fongkeng Beach (鳳坑海灘) in Hsinchu County’s Sinfong Township (新豐) from 8am to noon every day.
That follows the army’s Tianma exercise at the Kengzinkou Range (坑子口訓場) on Aug. 27, underscoring the increased training tempo of northern Taiwan’s anti-armor units.
The nation has conducted exercises since March, when the Second Combat Area in eastern Taiwan reopened a firing range at the mouth of Taitung County’s Taimali River (太麻里溪) for the first time in 30 years.
In June, the 6th Army Command conducted a live-fire drone and Tianma exercise in Yilan County, with an anti-armor platoon from the army’s 584th Combined Arms Brigade conducting qualification firing with TOW 2A missiles and validation firing with TOW 2B missiles.
The TOW 2B RF uses radio-frequency guidance rather than the wire guidance employed by the older TOW 2A, giving it a maximum range of 4,500m.
Its key feature is its top-attack capability: The missile flies above the target’s line of sight before detonating over an enemy tank and directing its warhead downward against the vehicle’s more vulnerable roof armor.
The command’s intensive top-attack drills at Fongkeng Beach are intended to bolster northern Taiwan’s coastal defenses and improve its ability to counter armored vehicles attempting an amphibious landing.

Taiwan Premier League set to kick off on Sunday
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:52 UTC
01:37:52 KST

The Taiwan Football Premier League (TFPL) is to start on Sunday, with four matches on the day, as clubs seek to dethrone Tainan City TSG as defending champions.
Eight teams are contesting the 10th season of Taiwan’s top men’s competition, with the Kaohsiung Attackers added to the roster after they won the second-division title last season, earning promotion to the top flight.
New Taipei Hang Yuan host TSG in the first game at the Fu Jen University Soccer Stadium in New Taipei City, while hosts Taichung Futuro take on the Tatung Taiwan Leopard Cats at Situn Soccer Stadium in Taichung.
Photo: CNA
Elsewhere, Taipower FC host Sunny Bank AC Taipei at the Nanzhih Soccer Stadium in Kaohsiung and the Attackers face Taichung Rock FC at the same ground in the evening match.
Players, coaches and officials of the Chinese Taipei Football Association (CTFA) governing body at a news conference on Tuesday last week unveiled the new season of 21 regular-season rounds, or 84 games, through May next year.
Officials said that the slogan for the season was “Beyond Limits.”
“This is an important milestone for the TFPL reaching its 10th year and we hope it will usher in a new era for Taiwan soccer,” CTFA chairman Michael Chang told the news conference.
The top men’s competition was once the national soccer league before turning semi-professional in the 1980s with the Enterprise Football League and rebranding as the Intercity Football League in 2007-2008. The TFPL launched in 2017-2018.
Chang said that the CTFA would push for more reforms, initiate new programs and plan for expansion of the TFPL.
“We are working toward adding two new teams to the current format so that 10 clubs are competing in the TFPL’s 2027-2028 season,” he said. “The plan is for each club to operate at its own home ground so it will be a full home-and-away competition,” he added.
The TFPL’s eight clubs are based in five major urban centers. Taipei (formerly the Leopard Cats), New Taipei City, Taichung, Tainan, and Kaohsiung (Taipower).
“Expanding would improve the competition and provide more opportunities for players,” Chang said. “Taiwan has many youngsters who are gaining experience at international tournaments, so the top-league TFPL is the stage for them to grow, cultivate and hone their skills, and challenge for higher honors.”
“That is the way Taiwan can sustain the future generations of soccer talent,” he added.
However, there are barriers, Chang said.
“Among the most urgent issues is the lack of fields that are up to the standard for a top-flight competition,” he said. “We must address this important task now, which requires the CTFA and all clubs to work toward upgrading pitches.”
Chang said that the sport needs more resources and funding from local governments, as well as more corporate sponsorship, citing the cost of booking certified soccer stadiums.
The Ministry of Sports should plan new stadiums dedicated to soccer, and provide more resources and funding to underwrite ground rental to reduce the financial burden on clubs, he said.
“Overall, we need more certified soccer grounds throughout Taiwan, for the men’s and women’s top-flight competitions, and also so we can host international tournaments,” he said.

INDONESIA
Japan helps fight wildfires
A Japanese military transport ship yesterday docked on the island of Borneo as part of a disaster relief mission to help fight wildfires that are causing a toxic haze impacting people’s health in other countries. Japan deployed 300 crew members, landing ship JS Kunisaki and three CH-47 helicopters, which arrived in Kalimantan. The mission marked the first known overseas firefighting operation carried out by the Japan Self-Defense Forces. “To this end, we will learn from the Indonesian military’s operational experience and work in coordination and cooperation with them, striving to ensure that the Indonesian people can lead stable lives as soon as possible,” Japanese Colonel Syunji Nakahara, the commander of the disaster relief activities, said at a port in Mempawah District.

NORTH KOREA
Kim could have another child
Leader Kim Jong-un’s daughter and apparent successor is believed to have a younger sibling, the South Korean National Intelligence Service said yesterday, offering a more detailed view of the ruling family’s line of succession. The spy agency has previously said Kim is thought to have three children, but some uncertainty remains on the number of offspring as well as the order of their birth. Kim’s daughter, Kim Ju-ae, was first introduced to the public in 2022 when she accompanied her father to the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile. Seoul had initially indicated that Kim Jong-un and his wife, Ri Sol-ju, had their first child, a boy, in 2010, and that Kim Ju-ae was their second child, but in 2023, Seoul said it was “unable to confirm” the existence of the son. The child described yesterday would be the youngest. “The National Intelligence Service currently assesses that Kim Ju-ae is being groomed as the successor and understands she has a younger sibling of unknown gender,” the agency said.

Authorities said he fled to his home after the shooting and police surrounded the house, where he remained until surrendering after an 18-hour standoff. All 44 students at the school were unharmed and evacuated with other teachers after the shooting.

Whaling ban expected
The government is to submit a bill in February to ban whaling, a move that would leave Norway and Japan as the only two countries in the world to continue commercial whaling. Whaling in Iceland has sparked years of protests from animal welfare campaigners and Hollywood celebrities. The bill would include “a permanent ban on whaling,” the government said on its Web site late on Wednesday. In this year’s hunting season, which runs from June to about the end of September, 80 fin whales were caught as of Wednesday, Humane World for Animals said. The quota allows 150 fin whales to be killed this year. “There is considerable political and public support for this bill to ban commercial whaling, and compelling ethical, veterinary, legal and conservation reasons to hope it succeeds,” Humane World for Animals spokeswoman Wendy Higgins said.

High court sentences two for developing CCP-linked organization
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:51 UTC
01:37:51 KST

The Taiwan High Court on Thursday sentenced Taiwanese businessman Cheng Ming- chia (鄭明嘉) to 10 years and six months in prison for developing an organization for the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) united front authorities.
Retired Executive Yuan official Hu Peng-nien (胡鵬年), meanwhile, was sentenced to five years for attempting to do the same.
The ruling can be appealed.
Photo :CNA
According to the court, from 2021 to 2025 Cheng helped CCP united front officials approach and attempt to recruit targets in Taiwan by providing contact information and arranging meetings in China.
He successfully recruited Hu as a potential operative, while his efforts to recruit another individual surnamed Huang (黃) failed after Huang did not respond.
Treating Cheng’s actions as a continuous offense, the court handed down a 10-year and six-month sentence.
Meanwhile, Hu used the same methods from 2021-2024 to try to recruit three people. None responded, leading the court to convict him of attempted development of an organization and hand down a sentence of five years in prison.
The court said Hu admitted to the offenses, while Cheng denied wrongdoing throughout the investigation and trial. It found the evidence against Cheng clear and rejected his defense.
Both defendants, the court said, followed instructions from CCP united front personnel to facilitate the recruitment of new targets.
Hu also transported a communications device supplied by the Chinese authorities into Taiwan and handed it to another person, conduct that the court said significantly aided Beijing’s united front efforts.
According to a January indictment by the Taiwan High Prosecutors’ Office, Cheng recruited Hu -- then teaching in China -- after becoming involved with CCP-affiliated united front organizations in Guangzhou, and arranged for him to take direction from CCP Taiwan affairs personnel in identifying contacts and recruits in Taiwan.
Prosecutors said Hu targeted current and retired military personnel, political workers, ward chiefs, retired civil servants and defense contractors, seeking military-related information and insights into government and legislative operations, though most recruitment efforts failed.
Cheng and Hu have remained in detention since their arrest following raids launched in September 2025, and both were absent from Thursday’s sentencing.

Samsung Electronics Co launched a publicity campaign for its foldable phones, touting its hardware advantage and its early entry into the segment as it seeks to fend off a major challenge from Apple Inc.
Apple on Wednesday unveiled the Duo, a folding US$1,999 iPhone aimed at shaking up a category long dominated by Samsung and Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co (華為), whose devices have struggled to move beyond a niche audience.
Apple adopted the passport-shaped design that Samsung Electronics unveiled less than two months ago with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, priced at US$1,899 and powered by Alphabet Inc’s Gemini artificial intelligence (AI).
Photo: Reuters
“Apple’s pricing was one of the most impressive parts. Keeping the iPhone Duo just under the US$2,000 mark, at US$1,999, and only about US$100 above the Galaxy Z Fold 8 looks like a pretty bold move by Apple,” Counterpoint Research associate director Liz Lee said.

The company also detailed its long-running efforts to reduce the weight of its foldable phones in a post on its Web site on Wednesday.
Responding to Apple’s launch on Wednesday, Samsung launched a flurry of sarcastic posts on X, mocking what it portrayed as a lack of meaningful innovation through taunts such as “reheating our leftovers” and “So far, so same.”

Samsung launched the first mass-market foldable phones in 2019, after initial setbacks as reviewers reported broken screens and other display issues, forcing a delayed rollout.
Since then, the South Korean company has launched eight generations of foldable phones, as it faces growing competition from Chinese rivals such as Huawei.
Apple is leveraging the supply chain Samsung has built for foldable phones, including foldable screens made by Samsung’s own unit, Samsung Display Co.

CWA warns of potentially deadly waves
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:46 UTC
01:37:46 KST

The Central Weather Administration (CWA) yesterday warned the public of potentially deadly hazards posed by swells, known locally as “crazy dog waves,” which have claimed more than 770 lives in the past 25 years.
From 2000 to November last year, the CWA recorded 445 incidents involving freak waves along Taiwan’s coasts, resulting in 778 people falling into the sea.
Offshore abnormal wave events were also reported, with 206 incidents recorded from 2000 to June 2023 involving 936 people, CWA data showed.
Photo: CNA
Lin Fang-ju (林芳如), a specialist in marine meteorological technology at the CWA’s Marine Meteorology and Climate Division, said long-period waves, or swells, can sometimes become hazardous.
The CWA has established separate warning systems for abnormal waves in coastal waters and the open ocean.
Wave conditions are primarily affected by wind speed, the size of the area over which the wind blows and the duration of the wind, Lin said.
Stronger winds blowing over a wider area for a longer period produce larger waves with greater energy, she said.
Wind waves are generated locally by winds blowing across the sea surface, while swells are generated by strong winds farther away and continue to travel after leaving the area affected by the winds, she added.
Swells are also known as long-period waves, Lin said.
Because swells have longer periods and travel faster than normal waves, they can reach speeds of more than 100kph, she said.
By comparison, typhoons generally move at about 5kph to 20kph. As a result, swells generated by a distant typhoon can reach Taiwan’s shores one or two days before the storm itself, she added.
When swells enter shallow waters, coastal topography can cause high waves that break and crash, creating dangerous conditions, she said, adding that unusually large waves despite calm local winds could indicate severe weather systems offshore.
The CWA provides real-time swell information when wave heights reach at least 1.5m and periods are eight seconds or longer, except during typhoon warnings.
In cooperation with National Cheng Kung University’s Coastal Hydraulics Center, the CWA has developed a Coastal Abnormal Wave Warning System to improve warnings of dangerous waves near shore.
The Ocean Abnormal Wave Warning System uses nonlinear wave theory and wave models to provide the probability of abnormal waves occurring in the following 24, 36 and 48 hours.
The CWA also uses data from buoys to monitor waves, currents, water temperatures, wind, air temperatures and atmospheric pressure.
The solar-powered buoys generally collect observations hourly when sufficient power is available, although fishing nets, ship collisions and ropes tied to the buoys can affect data quality.
In cooperation with Kenting National Park, the CWA provides warnings when forecast wave heights reach specified levels, and forecasts of high and low tide lines to help prevent people from becoming stranded on beaches or sandbars.

Bronze Age hoard, Egyptian diamonds: String of museum heists throughout August shake Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:44 UTC
01:37:44 KST

Nearly a year after the infamous Louvre heist shocked the world, a new series of museum thefts across Europe has raised concerns in the art and antiquities world about the rising phenomenon.
On Tuesday, four paintings were stolen from the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera, and in mid-August, four paintings by Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen from the Museo Regionale di Messina in the painter’s hometown.
Last month, the pan-European police body Europol said that art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad hoc opportunists recruited through social media.
But the recent heists have not only been of priceless paintings, but of artifacts as well.
Treasure of Villena
On August 27, thieves in Spain entered the Villena Museum (MUVI) and stole the majority of the Treasure of Villena, a collection of Bronze Age artifacts often described as one of the most significant prehistoric European finds.
The collection is made up of 66 artifacts of gold, silver, iron and amber. The gold artifacts including 11 bowls, three bottles and 28 bracelets.
It was originally discovered in 1963 by Spanish archaeologist José María Soler.
The theft happened “in a matter of minutes,” Villena Mayor Fulgencio Cerdán said during a press conference following the robbery.
He explained that the robbery took place around 5:20 a.m., with the thieves believed to have left the museum approximately four minutes later.
While most of the treasure had been taken, Cerdán noted that three silver vessels, a bracelet, some ornamentation of the bastón del reyezuelo, and the “Kingfisher staff.”
The stolen gold pieces are estimated to be worth €1.7 million, according to media reports.
“We are absolutely devastated,” Cerdán said. “I am shaking. The truth is that, for those of us from Villena, this destroys us. It is part of our heritage and part of our wealth and of what we feel proud of.”
Following the theft, MUVI stated in a social media post that it has temporarily closed its doors to the public, but will announce a reopening date as soon as possible.
“The MUVI's pieces and collections are not just heritage: they are shared memory, part of everyone's history,” the museum wrote. “We have full confidence in the ongoing investigations and the professionalism of the State Security Forces.”
Queen Nazli’s diamond necklace
That same day, two unmasked men smashed a display case at Vienna's Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) and stolen a diamond necklace worth over $4 million.
It had been featured at the MAK as part of an exhibition titled “GLANZSTÜCKE: Van Cleef & Arpels High Jewelry × Masterpieces from the MAK Collection.”
According to Austrian state broadcaster ORT, the unmasked thieves bought tickets to the exhibit prior to the robbery and commited the theft during the museum’s opening hours.
Police added that the two then “fled with the piece of jewelry in an unknown direction.”
Photographs and CCTV footage of the suspects have been shared by police, and has since been added to INTERPOL’s Stolen Works of Art database.
The museum noted in an August statement that it would not be sharing information regarding the investigation into the robbery.
Belonging once to Queen Nazli of Egypt (1913-1936), the second wife of King Fuad I, the necklace is adorned with 673 diamonds and weighs about 200 carats.
It, and a matching tiara, had been commissioned by Nazli for the wedding of her daughter Fawzia to, the at the time Iranian Crown Prince and later Shah, Mohammed Reza Pahlavi.
Reuters contributed to this report.

Australia jails man who compiled reports for China
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:42 UTC
01:37:42 KST

An Australian man convicted of reckless foreign interference for compiling reports for Chinese intelligence was yesterday sentenced to more than three years in jail by a Sydney court.
Marketing executive Alexander Csergo, 58, was arrested in Sydney by Australian police in 2023, shortly after he returned from living in Shanghai.
He was accused of accepting cash from Chinese intelligence agents to write reports on topics including Australia’s AUKUS nuclear submarine partnership with the US and the UK, and critical minerals.
Photo: Bianca De Marchi, AAP Image via AP
Sydney’s district court sentenced Csergo to three years and six months in jail, eligible for parole from next month, a court official said.
“Foreign interference is an assault on Australian sovereignty,” Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Director-General of Security Mike Burgess said, responding to the sentencing.
“In this case, the spies wanted the Australian to target individuals in Australia’s intelligence community, Prime Minister’s Office, defense sector, judiciary and think tanks,” he added.
Csergo is the second person to be convicted under foreign interference laws introduced in 2018 to criminalize activity that helps a foreign power interfere with Australia’s sovereignty or national interest.
He is the first person sentenced for reckless foreign interference.
The court heard that Csergo had met two suspected Chinese agents, known to him as Ken and Evelyn, in Shanghai after they made contact on professional networking platform LinkedIn.
He met the pair in empty cafes in Shanghai, where he suspected the venues had been cleared for their meetings.
He returned to Australia in 2023 with a “shopping list” of topics Ken wanted information collected on.
The police discovered the list three weeks after Csergo arrived in Australia to live with his family at Bondi Beach.
The court heard that Csergo exchanged thousands of WeChat messages with the pair between 2021 and 2023, and accepted cash in envelopes.
Csergo, found guilty by the court in March, had said that much of the information in the reports was publicly available.
The Australian Federal Police Assistant Commissioner Cyber and Special Investigations Sandra Booth said the best defense against foreign interference was community awareness.
“Often foreign powers will use covert, deceptive or coercive activities to influence political processes, harm national security or threaten communities,” she said.

Cabinet expands aid for long-term care
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:39 UTC
01:37:39 KST

The Executive Yuan yesterday approved expanded subsidies for residents of long-term care facilities, allocating NT$16.62 billion (US$526.82 million) to the plan expected to benefit about 105,000 people.
Under the new plan, the maximum monthly subsidy for people with moderate to severe disabilities residing in long-term care facilities would rise from NT$10,000 to NT$15,000, while the annual cap would increase from NT$120,000 to NT$180,000, the Cabinet said.
The program would accept applications under the updated scheme from Monday next week, with the subsidy adjustments applying retroactively from Jan. 1, it said.
Photo: CNA
The central government also plans to provide a monthly accommodation subsidy of NT$5,000 for people with moderate to severe physical or mental disabilities living in specialized disability care facilities, the Cabinet said.
Previously, eligibility for the program was assessed on an annual basis, with beneficiaries required to stay in a facility for more than 180 days to receive a full year’s subsidy. Those who stayed for fewer than 180 days were not eligible.
Under the revised scheme, subsidies would be calculated monthly, with applicants eligible for one month’s subsidy if they reside in a facility for at least half of the calendar days in a given month, the Cabinet said.
Eligible facilities include nursing homes, psychiatric nursing homes, senior welfare institutions, disability welfare institutions, veterans’ homes and long-term care service facilities.
The government would also shorten reimbursement times by increasing the disbursement schedule to twice a year, the Cabinet said.
Application, review and disbursement procedures have been streamlined to ensure faster and more stable payments, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) said.
The Ministry of Health and Welfare and local governments have been instructed to complete administrative preparations as soon as possible, and step up public outreach to ensure applications and reviews proceed smoothly and subsidies can be disbursed at the earliest opportunity, he said.
Taiwan has become a “super-aged” society, with the number of people aged 65 or older exceeding 4.77 million as of the end of July, accounting for 20.5 percent of the population, Cho said.
Of those 4.77 million, 16.47 percent have disabilities and 7.99 percent have dementia, Deputy Minister of Health and Welfare Lu Chien-te (呂建德) said.
To meet rapidly growing long-term care needs, the government this year launched the Long-Term Care 3.0 program, investing NT$115.3 billion in its first year, Cho said.
The program aims to enhance coordination between medical and care services, while expanding support for people with moderate to severe disabilities and their families, he said.
The health ministry’s revised scheme would focus on reducing financial burdens and streamlining administrative procedures, he added.

Cabinet approves draft for NT$100bn MSME program
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
16:37:39 UTC
01:37:39 KST

The Executive Yuan yesterday approved a draft proposal for an eight-year, NT$100 billion (US$3.17 billion) program to support the development of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) through expanded tax breaks, relaxed investment thresholds and targeted loans.
More than 4,000 MSMEs are expected to benefit from the initiative, generating more than NT$50 billion in investment, the Ministry of Economic Affairs said.
A notice to commence a period of public comments for the proposal was announced yesterday, with public hearings to be held to gather feedback from business owners.
Photo: Chung Li-hua, Taipei Times
It is expected to be submitted to the Executive Yuan for approval next month before being forwarded to the legislature for review.
According to the government’s White Paper on Small and Medium Enterprises last year, Taiwan has 1.716 million MSMEs, accounting for 98.9 percent of all businesses and employing nearly 80 percent of the workforce, or about 9.194 million people.
The draft plans to extend government assistance to 1.029 million microbusinesses, including sole proprietorships and partnerships, which account for about 60 percent of all businesses.
The program would also cover commercial districts, public markets, local specialty industries, agricultural enterprises, tourism businesses and start-ups.
It includes measures to improve the business environment in 353 commercial districts and 1,030 public markets.
A chapter dedicated to start-up development discussed encouraging large corporations and venture capital firms to nurture start-ups, and creating an environment for innovation and experimentation. Larger companies would be encouraged to help MSMEs connect with high-tech supply chains and digital platforms.
For businesses with fewer than 30 employees, the government would provide simplified loan applications, project-based loans and short-term interest subsidies, while expanding credit guarantee coverage.
A Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Fund would also increase its risk coverage to help smaller businesses that lack substantial collateral to obtain financing for transformation.
Businesses could obtain additional credit guarantee coverage if funds are used to raise employee wages, the ministry said.
The program would significantly expand tax incentives for equipment investment, and research and development (R&D), and lower the minimum investment required to qualify for tax credits on smart machinery, artificial intelligence, digital transformation and net zero equipment from NT$1 million to NT$250,000, under the Industrial Innovation Act (產業創新條例).
Digital management systems needed by service businesses and outsourced R&D spending would also qualify for the first time, while the R&D tax credit rate would rise to 20 percent.
Tax incentives for hiring would be expanded, with the eligible age range widened from 24 or younger and 65 or older to 29 or younger and 55 or older.
The additional tax deduction for wage increases would rise from 175 to 200 percent.

BASEBALL
Japanese legend dies at 86
Japanese baseball legend Isao Harimoto, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and became the first player from his country to reach 3,000 hits, has died aged 86, reports said yesterday. Born to Korean parents in Japan, Harimoto learned to play left-handed when an accident at the age of four left him with severe burns and limited mobility in his right hand. He survived the atomic bombing as a five-year-old, his mother jumping in front of him and his sister to shield them from the blast. He went on to rack up 3,085 career hits, which still stands as a record in Nippon Professional Baseball. He played for several teams in Japan, including the all-powerful Yomiuri Giants, and earned himself the nickname “Hit Machine” for his batting prowess.
